MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
March 4, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday,
March 4, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present
were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community
Services Director McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation
Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Gazeley seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. PRESENTATIONS

Kathy McCune, Metro Transportation Planning Manager, provided a PowerPoint presentation
regarding the Metro Express Lanes on 110 Harbor Freeway. Ms. McCune stated that all
drivers need a FasTrak transponder in order to use the Express Lanes, however, carpools
with two or more people, vanpools, and motorcycles with a FasTrak transponder will travel
the Express Lanes toll-free. According to Ms. McCune, the main goal of the FasTrak project
is to move more people by offering more transportation choices. Ms. McCune explained to
those in attendance how to sign up for a FasTrak account and receive a transponder, as well
as how the FasTrak system distinguishes between solo drivers and carpools when charging
tolls. Ms. McCune also provided an overview of the fees and citations assessed for those
using the Express Lanes without a FasTrak account/transponder.

Councilmembers Gazeley and Savidan stated that they both use FasTrak, which is very
convenient and saves significant time in commuting. Councilmember Traina stated that he
opposes all toll roads and supports freeways being open to everyone, as toll lanes are
basically a double charge for taxpayers.

  Page 1 of 6
 4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that he would be on a ride along with
Deputy Lopez on Friday, March 8, 2013.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina stated that City Council and staff need to start planning for obtaining
a second well somewhere in the City of Lomita, as well as looking for opportunities with the
Water Replenishment District to help with implementing a reverse osmosis process at our
treatment plant. Councilmember Traina added that the City needs to plan for the next
generation, and not rely on just one well.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that on February 20th and 21st, 2013, he attended the
Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting in Sacramento, where he
met with State Senator Ted Lieu and State Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi. Councilmember
Gazeley also stated that he and City Manager Rock attended a meeting of the South Bay
Council of Governments in Carson, on February 22, 2013. And finally, Councilmember
Gazeley reported that he threw out the first pitch at the Lomita Little League on March 2,
2013; Councilmember Gazeley stated that it was a nice event and thanked the parents for
the work they do on the Lomita Little League Field.

Councilmember Savidan reported that a week and half ago the Lomita Helicopter Noise
Subcommittee held a meeting and met with a couple of residents from Torrance who serve
on similar committees. Councilmember Savidan added that they have already started to see
some improvements regarding the helicopter noise issue.

Councilmember Sanchez asked staff to post the minutes of the Planning Commission in a
more timely manner, and added that the minutes from the February 11, 2013, meeting of the
Planning Commission have not yet been posted on the City’s website.

Mayor Estrada reported that she attended a meeting of the California League of Cities and
had a very productive conversation with State Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi regarding
Lomita issues, such as the lack of funding for street improvement projects, massage parlors,
and helicopter noise. Mayor Estrada also stated that she asked Assemblymember
Muratsuchi for assistance in funding for the rehabilitation of the Stephenson Center and
expansion of the Lomita Railroad Museum.

6.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Miguel Cordova, Senior Field Representative for State Assemblyman Al Muratsuchi, informed
those in attendance that he will be the liaison for Lomita, and provided the contact
information for the Assemblyman's new District Office: 3460 Torrance Boulevard, Suite 306,
in Torrance; 310-316-2164 (land line); and 916-302-6226 (cell phone). Mr. Cordova also
invited everyone to attend the District Office's Open House on Thursday, March 7, 2013,
from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked

  Page 2 of 6
   Councilmember Gazeley for attending the Business Mixer at the Lomita Magnet School. Mr.
  Kivett also invited those in attendance to the Chamber's next Business Mixer on Thursday,
  March 21, 2013, which will take place at the Lomita Library, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.
  Finally, Mr. Kivett welcomed AAA Sewing and Fabric, located on Pacific Coast Highway, as a
  new Chamber member.

  7. CONSENT AGENDA

  Councilmember Gazeley asked that Item 7.B be pulled from the Consent Agenda for
  discussion. Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember
  Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  In response to Councilmember Gazeley's inquiry regarding Item 7.B, on whether the vision,
  mission, and core values were going to be brought back for discussion and City Council
  approval, City Manager Rock stated that the vision, mission, and core values would be
  brought back to the Council on March 18, 2013 for consideration. Councilmember Gazeley
  moved to approve Item 7.B. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
  unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council on February 13,
  2013, and the Regular City Council meeting held on February 19, 2013. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. January 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  PUBLIC HEARING

  8. STATUS OF THE TREE COMMISSION: Consideration of an Ordinance of the City
  Council of the City of Lomita deleting Chapter 17 of Title 2 in its entirety by dissolving the
  City of Lomita Tree Commission, amending Section 2-10.08 (Duties and Responsibilities
  of the Parks and Recreation Commission) by adding additional responsibilities related to
  city trees, and amending Section 2-5.020 (D) (Definitions).

City Manager Rock informed City Council that he attended the last meeting of the Tree
Commission to discuss potential transfer of certain duties from the Tree Commission to the
Parks and Recreation Commission. According to City Manager Rock there are several reasons

  Page 3 of 6
 why consolidation of the two commissions is logical, two of which are that the Tree Commission
agendas are relatively light, and that the Public Works Department is understaffed, thereby
making it difficult for the Department to handle the workload. City Manager Rock added that in
the past, some duties and decision-making was delegated to the Tree Commission, but should
have been handled by the Public Works Department, in accordance with the Lomita Municipal
Code.

Councilmember Traina inquired as to the feedback received from the Tree Commissioners
regarding potential consolidation, to which City Manager replied that some of the feedback was
positive, while some Commissioners disagreed with the recommendation to consolidate the two
Commissions. Responding to Councilmember Sanchez’s question regarding the staff support
and the financial impact of the Tree Commission, City Manager Rock stated that the Tree
Commission involves overtime, as well as the preparation of minutes, posting of agendas and
follow-up by staff on action items.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing.

DeeAnne Sathe, Lomita resident and former Tree Commissioner, informed the City Council that
she has served as a Tree Commissioner since 2007, and had been the Chair of the Tree
Commission for the last four years. Ms. Sathe also stated that she resigned at the last meeting
of the Tree Commission. Ms. Sathe continued by expressing her concerns regarding the lack of
response by Public Works staff to resident requests, and the refusal by the Council to consider
the Lomita Pines boundaries. Ms. Sathe concluded by stating that the Tree Commission gives
residents the opportunity to to be heard, and that institutional knowledge would be lost if the two
Commissions are consolidated.

Robert Stemmer, Tree Commissioner, thanked DeeAnn Sathe for an outstanding job as a Tree
Commissioner and Chair of the Commission. According to Mr. Stemmer, the Lomita Pines
boundaries are important, to which he stated nobody wants to take ownership of or address the
issues associated with those boundaries. Mr. Stemmer suggested that instead of consolidation,
have the Tree Commission meet less frequently. Furthermore, Mr. Stemmer asked the Council
to re-consider agendizing the Lomita Pines boundaries, which was pulled from the Consent
Agenda on January 3, 2012.

Mayor Estrada closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Gazeley made a motion to introduce the first reading of an Ordinance deleting
Title II, Chapter 17 (Tree Commission) of the Lomita Municipal Code, and amending Title II,
Chapter 10 of the Lomita Municipal Code (Parks and Recreation Commission) by adding
additional responsibilities and deleting reference to the Tree Commission in Title II, Chapter 5
(Revolving Door Ordinance). Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion.

Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez stated that they would like the Tree Commission to
continue, perhaps with less frequent meetings as suggested. Councilmember Traina also
added that the Tree Commission and the Parks and Recreation Commission have different
areas of expertise, and that consolidating the two Commissions does not seem logical.

ROLL CALL:
AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada

  Page 4 of 6
 NOES: Councilmembers Sanchez and Traina

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

  9. INDEPENDENTLY AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2011/12
  Presentation of the Independently Audited Financial Statements for Fiscal Year 2011/12 by
  Gruber and Associates and approval of Fiscal Year 2011/12 Comprehensive Annual
  Financial Audit (CAFR). Presented by Ron Lopez, Gruber and Associates.

Ron Lopez, Partner at Gruber and Associates, informed the City Council that Gruber and
Associates audited the accompanying financial statements of governmental activities, the
business type activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information of the
City of Lomita for the year ended June 30, 2012, and has issued a clean unqualified opinion.
Mr. Lopez provided an overview of net assets and revenues, and noted that the reduction of
$669,394 in net asserts is associated with Water Fund expenses, which should show
improvement next year as the Cypress Water Production Facility becomes operational.

Mr. Lopez stated that one finding had been identified in the federal program, which had also
been identified during the prior audit by the Department of Housing and Urban Development
(HUD) in May 2012. According to Mr. Lopez, staff of Gruber and Associates has made
recommendations to resolve the issues in that program, and that the letter of response sent to
HUD had been accepted, and that the auditors were pleased with the results.

Mr. Lopez continued by stating that Gruber and Associates encountered no difficulties while
performing the audit, and that there were no audit adjustments or disagreement with
management. Mr. Lopez concluded by stating that Gruber and Associates made a few non-
material recommendations, which were mostly housekeeping items, like the creation of a
Finance Committee.

Councilmember Traina moved to receive and file the report.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  10. DISCUSSION  OF  APPEAL  PROCEDURES  FOR  PLANNING  COMMISSION
  DECISIONS

Assistant City Manager Sugano briefly explained the current procedure for appealing Planning
Commission decisions: any member of the public may appeal a decision of the Planning
Commission within 15 days, however, City Council cannot appeal decisions of the Planning
Commission, due to the changes made to the Lomita Municipal Code in 2010, which removed
the provision allowing the majority of City Council to appeal Planning Commission decisions.

City Attorney Hogin explained the difference between the legislative and the administrative roles
of the City Council. According to City Attorney Hogin, Council acting in the administrative role
has less leeway in the decision-making process, as specific rules must be applied to specific
sets of tasks in order to make unbiased decisions. City Attorney Hogin further explained that the
issue with Council making its own appeal gets in the way of Council maintaining its neutrality, as
Council should avoid the perception of prejudging decisions. Given the above, City Attorney
Hogin outlined several options that City Council could consider: (1) eliminate Council from the
appeal process completely; (2) have every Planning Commission decision approved by Council,
thereby making the Planning Commission an advisory board; (3) Council could appeal to itself
  Page 5 of 6
 without expressing the reasons why they are making an appeal; or (4) empower each
Councilmember or a majority of Councilmembers to file an appeal, which according to City
Attorney Hogin is the least preferred option, as it creates a problem for individual
councilmembers and could be perceived as pre-judgment. Prior to selecting any option, City
Attorney Hogin recommended the Council first decide what role they would like the Planning
Commission to play.

Discussion followed as to whether this particular information was part of the discussion in 2010,
when the Lomita Municipal Code was amended and appeal provisions removed.
Councilmember Sanchez expressed concern that Council typically receives minutes from
Planning Commission meetings after the expiration of the appeal process, and in turn asked
whether the minutes could be prepared earlier in order to inform Council about Planning
Commission decisions. City Attorney Hogin responded to Councilmember Sanchez's inquiry by
explaining that minutes of the Planning Commission are approved at the next regularly
scheduled meeting, and the Planning Commission meets once a month. Assistant City
Manager Sugano added that staff does provide Council with an Annotated Agenda, or Action
Summary, immediately after a Planning Commission meeting.

Discussion followed regarding the Council's role in the appeal process, and whether Council
would like to consider giving themselves the opportunity to appeal Planning Commission
decisions.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, reminded Council of the entitlement process, and stated that
extending the appeal process would in turn extend contingencies for an applicant, and
potentially have negative effects.

Councilmember Sanchez made a motion to bring back the information relayed by the City
Attorney to Council for discussion so that a determination could be made at a later date.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:21 p.m., in memory of Gabriel Paz and Chris Middlekoff.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
